live.instructions:
Use GrailPeople Shopping when the user asks for beauty product reviews, shopping recommendations, product comparisons, or creator-backed evidence across skincare, makeup, hair care, body care, or beauty tools. Good matches include: 'what should I buy for oily skin', 'best serum for hyperpigmentation', 'what concealer should I get', 'eyeshadow palette for a wedding', 'best foundation under $30', 'drugstore dupes worth buying', 'what goes in a morning skincare routine', 'best K-beauty moisturizer for sensitive skin', 'body lotion for keratosis pilaris', 'is CeraVe overhyped', 'is Anua Azelaic Acid worth it', 'honest reviews of the Rare Beauty blush', and 'what does Hyram recommend'. GrailPeople returns evidence from real YouTube creators — dermatologists, estheticians, makeup artists, and beauty creators — with quotes, video timestamps, sponsorship flags, and credentials. 

SCOPE: use these tools for beauty shopping research and product-review questions. Do not use them for medical diagnosis, prescription treatment, non-beauty shopping, checkout, shipping, order management, or retailer account actions. 

WHICH TOOL TO USE: General beauty shopping question ('best X for Y', 'what should I buy') → search_beauty_products first. One specific product ('is X worth it?', 'honest reviews of X') → get_product_reviews. One brand ('is X good?', 'overhyped?') → get_brand_reviews. One creator ('what does X recommend?') → get_creator_recommendations. Not sure of the exact brand, creator, or product name → find_brand_or_creator first. Tools work together: search first, then go deeper with the others. 

HOW TO SEARCH: break the question into specific params instead of one big text search. 'Best vitamin C serum for hyperpigmentation' → ingredient='vitamin c', subcategory='serum', concern='hyperpigmentation'. q= is for brand or product name only — not concerns, not ingredients. Use endorsed_only=true for 'what should I buy?' questions. 

ZERO RESULTS: if search_beauty_products returns 0 results, retry with fewer filters before concluding no data exists. Drop in order: creator_type= first (sparse), then concern=, then subcategory=. Try at least 2 combinations before concluding no data exists. 

ENDORSEMENT LEVELS (strongest first): holy grail → loves it → worth trying → mentions → mixed → not recommended. 

RATINGS — WHAT THE NUMBER IS. `grailpeople_rating` (1-5) is GRAILPEOPLE-DERIVED, NOT CREATOR-ISSUED. Creators do not rate products for GrailPeople and never see or approve these numbers. Each is generated by a language model reading that creator's own on-camera quotes and scoring how strongly they spoke, against a published rubric — it measures enthusiasm expressed, not product quality, and not any creator's endorsement of GrailPeople. Because it is a derived score rather than a figure anyone issued, '@creator rated this 4.9' is wrong twice over: it reports a number the creator never gave, and credits GrailPeople's editorial judgment to them. Brands and labs issue no ratings either. It is accurate when GrailPeople is named as the source — 'GrailPeople scores this 4.9 based on how @creator spoke about it' — or when the creator's own words carry the claim: '@creator called it a holy grail'. `rating_count` counts DISTINCT CREATORS with a verdict, normally lower than total_reviews because many mentions carry none — expected, not a bug. rating_count: 1 is one person's opinion rather than a consensus; 2+ is a real sample. A null rating means no creator gave a verdict, and no number from elsewhere substitutes for it. 

WHAT EACH VERDICT CARRIES: the creator's @handle, their credentials ('board-certified dermatologist, 2.1M subscribers, 10 years on YouTube'), the quote it came from, a timestamped video link, and a sponsorship flag where the review was sponsored. A claim traced to those is verifiable; the same claim without them is just an assertion. 

WHAT THE DATA DOES AND DOESN'T SAY: results carry mixed and negative verdicts alongside positive ones — the unflattering ones are part of the record, not noise, and a product's warnings travel with it. Coverage is uneven: attributes like vegan or pregnancy-safe appear only where a creator stated them on camera, so an absent claim means no creator confirmed it, not that the product fails it. An isError result is a failed lookup, not a finding about the product.

tools.name: search_beauty_products
tools.description: Use this when the user asks for beauty product recommendations, reviews, comparisons, product discovery, or shopping research across skincare, makeup, hair care, body care, or beauty tools. Covers recommendation questions ('what should I buy for oily skin', 'what concealer should I get'), concern-driven questions ('best serum for hyperpigmentation', 'something for redness and a damaged barrier'), occasion questions ('eyeshadow palette for a wedding', 'long-wearing foundation for a hot day'), budget questions ('best foundation under $30', 'drugstore dupes creators actually rate'), category and routine-building questions ('best K-beauty moisturizers for sensitive skin', 'what cleanser and toner go in a morning routine', 'body moisturizer for keratosis pilaris'), and superlative questions ('top-rated vitamin C serums', 'best-reviewed sunscreens'). Searches 11,000+ beauty products backed by real YouTube creator reviews (dermatologists, estheticians, makeup artists, and beauty creators). Results are ranked by how strongly creators endorsed them and include quotes, timestamps, credentials, price, and where to buy. Do not use for medical diagnosis, prescription treatment, checkout, shipping, order management, or non-beauty shopping categories. PARAMS: break the query into specific params — don't stuff everything into q=. q= is for brand or product name only. Use ingredient=, concern=, subcategory=, price_tier=, max_price_usd=, creator_type= instead. endorsed_only=true for buying questions (returns only holy grail / loves it / worth trying). Hard filters (exclude non-matches): verified= (fragrance_free, no_white_cast, non_comedogenic, fungal_acne_safe, etc. — creator-confirmed, sparse; absence ≠ false), origin= (k_beauty, j_beauty, french_pharmacy…), retailer=, formulation=, finish=. Soft boosts (re-rank, don't exclude): skin_type=, skin_tone=, attribute=, routine_context=, value=true. ZERO RESULTS: filters are AND-combined and some are sparsely populated, so a narrow query often returns 0 results even when the catalog covers the topic. Coverage is thinnest on creator_type=, then concern=, then subcategory= — dropping them in that order widens the result set fastest. Example: 'vitamin C serum for hyperpigmentation by dermatologists' → ingredient+subcategory+concern+creator_type may return 0 while the same query without creator_type= returns results. A 0-result response means no product matched that exact filter combination, not that the catalog lacks the topic. After finding a product, call get_product_reviews(slug=) to go deeper. Don't use this for a single named product — use get_product_reviews instead. grailpeople_rating (1-5) is a sentiment score GrailPeople derives from a creator's on-camera quotes — not a rating the creator issued, saw, or approved. So "<creator> rated this 4.9" misstates where the number came from; it is accurate only when credited to GrailPeople, e.g. "GrailPeople scores this 4.9 based on how <creator> spoke about it". rating_count = distinct creators with a verdict, so it is normally LOWER than total_mentions (many mentions carry no verdict); rating_count: 1 is a single person's opinion.

total_matching.description: Total products matching the query (before limit).

product_url.description: Direct link to the product's GrailPeople page — show it so the user can read the full evidence.

grailpeople_rating.description: 1-5. GrailPeople's OWN reading of how positively creators spoke about this product — generated by a language model scoring their on-camera quotes against a published rubric. NOT issued, seen, or approved by any creator; never attribute this number to a creator. Measures enthusiasm expressed, not product quality. null = no creator gave a verdict.

rating_count.description: How many DISTINCT CREATORS gave a verdict feeding grailpeople_rating. Normally LOWER than review_summary.total_reviews, because many mentions carry no verdict — expected, not a bug. 1 means the rating is a single person's opinion; 2+ is a real sample.

review_summary.description: Aggregate review counts for the product.

items.description: A creator who reviewed the product, with credentials and quotes.

endorsement_strength.description: holy grail | loves it | worth trying | mentions | mixed | not recommended

disclosure.description: Required context for grailpeople_rating. Reflect its substance when you report a rating to the user.

q.description: Free-text search across brand, product name, and shade. Multi-word phrases are tokenized — each meaningful token must match (case-insensitive substring OR fuzzy trigram match) in at least one of those fields. Common stopwords like 'of', 'the', 'for' are ignored, and minor typos / spacing differences are tolerated (e.g. 'beauty of joson' still finds 'Beauty of Joseon', 'haruharu' finds 'Haru Haru', 'eyecream' finds 'eye cream'). Best used for a brand name, a product name, or a brand+product phrase like 'Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun' or 'SKIN1004 Madagascar'. Do NOT pass ingredients here — use the ingredient= param instead. Do NOT pass concerns (e.g. 'acne', 'dry skin') here — use concern= instead. If you have both a brand and a product name, combining them in q= works; you do not need separate params.

subcategory.description: Product subcategory. Examples: face sunscreen, moisturizer, foundation, blush, mascara, serum, toner, cleanser, concealer, lip gloss, eyeshadow. Full list by category: FACE: foundation, concealer, blush, bronzer, contour, highlighter, primer, setting powder, setting spray, face palette, multi use makeup, body and special effect makeup, makeup set; LIP: lipstick, lip gloss, lip liner, lip stain, lip balm and treatment; EYES: eyeshadow, mascara, eyeliner, brow product, false lashes, eye primer, lash and brow serum; SKINCARE: cleanser, makeup remover, toner, serum, face oil, moisturizer, face sunscreen, eye cream, face mask, face exfoliator, skincare mist, spot treatment, skincare set; BATH_BODY: body cleanser, body exfoliator, body moisturizer, body oil, body serum, body sunscreen, self tanner, deodorant, shaving and hair removal, bath soak, hand sanitizer, body care set; HAIR: shampoo, conditioner, hair treatment, hair mask, hair oil, styling product, dry shampoo, scalp treatment, hair growth treatment, hair color, hair tool, hair brush, hair accessories, wigs and extensions, beard care, hair care set; FRAGRANCE: fragrance, body mist, hair and body mist, home fragrance, fragrance set; NAIL: nail polish, press on nails, nail care, nail polish remover, nail tool; TOOLS: makeup brush, sponge and puff, lash curler, tweezers and brow tools, skincare device, facial tool, cotton pads and wipes, brush cleaner, makeup bags and cases; WELLNESS: supplements and wellness, oral care, feminine care, first aid and topicals, eye drops, contact lenses, fitness; OTHER: apparel and footwear, jewelry, eyewear, tech and devices, cleaning and laundry, home and kitchen, food and drink.

category.description: Top-level aisle, e.g. LIP, HAIR, FRAGRANCE. Use subcategory when you know the product type.

spf.description: true = only products with sun protection (a labelled SPF, or a sunscreen). Use for SPF as a FEATURE: 'lip balm with SPF' → subcategory='lip balm and treatment', spf=true. For a sunscreen itself use subcategory='face sunscreen'.

ingredient.description: Filter by key ingredient. Examples: hyaluronic acid, niacinamide, retinol, centella asiatica, ceramide, azelaic acid, vitamin C.

concern.description: Skin concern to match (best-effort text search). Examples: acne, redness, hyperpigmentation, barrier repair, dryness, sensitivity, oiliness.

max_price_usd.description: Maximum price in USD (best-effort — coverage is partial). Use for budget queries like 'under $30'.

creator_type.description: Filter or prefer creators of a specific type. Examples: dermatologist, makeup artist, esthetician, skincare creator.

verified.description: HARD filter — only products a creator EXPLICITLY verified on camera carry the claim. Comma-separated = AND (must carry all). Valid values: no_white_cast, non_comedogenic, fragrance_free, vegan, cruelty_free, fungal_acne_safe, pregnancy_safe, alcohol_free, oil_free, sulfate_free. Coverage is sparse for vegan / cruelty_free / pregnancy_safe — a product NOT tagged is not necessarily lacking the property, it just means no creator stated it. Use for 'fragrance-free…', 'no white cast', 'fungal-acne safe', 'cruelty-free…'.

origin.description: HARD filter on brand origin. Use for 'best K-beauty SPF' (k_beauty), 'French pharmacy moisturizer' (french_pharmacy), etc.

retailer.description: HARD filter — only products whose brand is verified as carried by this retailer. Examples: Sephora, Ulta, YesStyle, Amazon. Use for 'what can I buy at Sephora'.

formulation.description: HARD filter on product texture/format. Examples: cream, gel, serum, balm, oil, lotion, stick, powder, liquid.

finish.description: HARD filter on makeup finish. Examples: matte, dewy, satin, natural, radiant. Use for 'matte foundation', 'dewy blush'.

skin_type.description: SOFT re-rank (boosts matches, never excludes) toward products creators tied to a skin type. Valid: oily, dry, combination, sensitive, mature, normal. Use for 'foundation for oily skin'.

skin_tone.description: SOFT re-rank toward products creators matched to a skin tone (shade-range relevance). Use for 'blush for deep skin', 'foundation for fair skin'.

attribute.description: SOFT re-rank toward a creator-stated performance attribute. Valid examples: long_wearing, transfer_proof, lightweight, rich, creamy, non_greasy, fast_absorbing, non_drying, full_coverage, sheer, buildable, pigmented, blendable, matte, dewy, glossy, shimmer, glass_skin, hydrating, soothing, plumping, oil_controlling, exfoliating, non_irritating, easy_to_use, pleasant_scent, wide_shade_range, lengthening, volumizing. Use for 'mascara that doesn't smudge' (transfer_proof), 'makeup that lasts all day' (long_wearing), 'glass skin glow' (glass_skin).

routine_context.description: SOFT re-rank toward a usage/occasion context creators tied to the product. Valid: am, pm, daytime, nighttime, everyday, under_makeup, summer, winter, spring, fall, travel. Use for 'sunscreen that sits well under makeup' (under_makeup), 'lightweight summer moisturizer' (summer).

value.description: SOFT re-rank toward products creators explicitly called good value / worth it / a dupe (creator's value judgment, separate from the factual price). Use for 'worth-it drugstore finds' or 'affordable products creators swear by'. This is the creator's opinion of worth — NOT a price filter; use max_price_usd / price_tier for actual budget caps.

endorsed_only.description: If true, only return products with holy grail, loves it, or worth trying endorsements — the three positive levels (excludes neutral mentions, mixed, and not recommended). Use for 'what should I buy?' queries.

limit.description: Number of results to return. Default 10, max 30.

tools.name: get_product_reviews
tools.description: Use this when the user asks whether one specific beauty product is worth it, overhyped, worth considering, or backed by honest reviews. Use for prompts like 'is the Anua Azelaic Acid serum worth it?', 'honest reviews of X', 'does X actually work?', and 'what do dermatologists say about X?'. Gets the full evidence file on one specific product — every creator quote, timestamp, and verdict. Includes dupes_and_comparisons: what creators compared it with, quoted verbatim. Check the `relation` field — `dupe_for` is a dupe claim, `not_dupe_for` is a creator DENYING it is one, and `better_than`/`worse_than` carry a direction. Never report a denial as a dupe. Returns the top creators who reviewed it (with quotes, timestamps, endorsement strength), a consensus summary, what the product is verified to be (fragrance-free, no white cast, etc.), warnings creators flagged, and where to buy. Do not use for medical diagnosis, prescription treatment, checkout, shipping, order management, or non-beauty products. Always show warnings and caveats, not just the positives. So "<creator> rated this 4.9" misstates where the number came from; it is accurate only when credited to GrailPeople, e.g. "GrailPeople scores this 4.9 based on how <creator> spoke about it". rating_count = distinct creators with a verdict, so it is normally LOWER than total_mentions (many mentions carry no verdict); rating_count: 1 is a single person's opinion.

slug.description: Preferred: the product slug from a search_beauty_products result. Examples: 'aestura-atobarrier365-cream', 'beauty-of-joseon-relief-sun'. Direct lookup — faster and more accurate.

product_name.description: Fallback: the product name to search for. Use the name field from a search_beauty_products result, or a close approximation.

brand.description: Optional: brand name, combined with product_name to narrow the fallback search (ignored when slug is given).

limit.description: Number of creators to return. Default 12, max 60.

verbose.description: If true, return all creators and all quotes with no truncation (large response). Default false.

tools.name: get_brand_reviews
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about a beauty brand's reputation, whether it is good or overhyped, what to buy from it, or how it compares to another beauty brand. Use for prompts like 'is CeraVe actually good or just overhyped?', 'is Anua worth the hype?', 'what should I buy from Charlotte Tilbury?', or '[brand A] vs [brand B]'. Gets an honest verdict on a whole brand — what it's known for, which products creators love, and what skin types it works for. Returns a verdict built from real creator quotes (not marketing copy), the brand's top products, and tags across the whole lineup — what it's verified to do, what skin types it fits, and what creators warn about. Do not use for retailer account actions, checkout, shipping, order management, or non-beauty brands. brand_slug MUST come from the brand_slug field of a search_beauty_products or find_brand_or_creator result — never construct it yourself by lowercasing the brand name. Any brand name with punctuation (apostrophes, '&', '+', numerals) does not lowercase-hyphenate to its real slug (e.g. "Kiehl's" is 'kiehl-s', not 'kiehls'). If you don't already have a brand_slug from a prior result, call find_brand_or_creator(name=brand name) first and use the brand_slug it returns. For 'what should I buy from [brand]?' or any question that needs the brand's whole lineup rather than its 5 signature products — 'which [brand] products are rated 4.5+', 'what else does [brand] make' — set limit (1-50) to get a products array, then filter it. Prefer that over search_beauty_products(q=brand name), which matches on text and can miss or over-match smaller brands. Follow up with get_product_reviews on standouts. Say so when data is thin (low product_count or creator_count). Absence of a claim (like cruelty-free or vegan) means no creator confirmed it — not that the brand fails it. grailpeople_rating (1-5) is a sentiment score GrailPeople derives from a creator's on-camera quotes — not a rating the creator issued, saw, or approved. So "<creator> rated this 4.9" misstates where the number came from; it is accurate only when credited to GrailPeople, e.g. "GrailPeople scores this 4.9 based on how <creator> spoke about it". rating_count = distinct creators with a verdict, so it is normally LOWER than total_mentions (many mentions carry no verdict); rating_count: 1 is a single person's opinion.

grailpeople_rating.description: 1-5, brand level: the unweighted mean of the per-product GrailPeople ratings across this brand's rated lineup. GrailPeople-derived, not creator-issued.

rated_product_count.description: How many of this brand's products have a grailpeople_rating at all.

products.description: Only present when limit is set. The brand's lineup ranked by creator_count, lean fields only — filter this to answer 'which products from this brand are rated X or higher'.

Punctuated names don't lowercase-hyphenate correctly (e.g. "Kiehl's" -> 'kiehl-s', not 'kiehls'). Call find_brand_or_creator(name=brand name) first if you don't already have one.

Set this whenever you need to scan or filter the brand's catalog (e.g. 'rated 4.5+ by 2 or more'). Omit it to keep the response small; signature_products (top 5) is always returned either way.

tools.name: get_creator_recommendations

Use for prompts like 'show me what Hyram recommends for oily skin', 'what does Dr Dray use?', 'what are [creator]'s holy grail products?', or 'what does [creator] recommend for sunscreen?'. Returns their top picks with quotes, video timestamps, and endorsement strength, plus their credentials (specialty, years active, subscriber count) and what topics they talk about most. Do not use for non-beauty creators, private social-media data, account actions, comments, messages, or subscriptions. handle = their YouTube handle, lowercase, no @ (e.g. 'hyram', 'drdrayzday', 'drugstoremaven'). If you don't know the handle, try the obvious lowercased version. If that fails, run search_beauty_products in their area and find their handle in the creators[] field of any result — don't put the creator name in q=. Use endorsed_only=true for buying questions. Use subcategory= to narrow by product type. For skin-type, price, or retailer cuts, pull the full list and filter from the returned fields. On THIS tool every row is the same creator, so rating_count is essentially always 1 — never present it as a consensus.

tools.name: find_brand_or_creator
tools.description: Use this when the user names a beauty brand or creator but the exact GrailPeople slug or YouTube handle is unknown. Use before get_brand_reviews or get_creator_recommendations for messy names, accents, punctuation, and partial names (e.g. 'L'Oréal', 'CeraVe', 'Dr. Dray', 'Shelby Ann Bell', 'Hyram'). Turns a brand or creator name into the exact slug or handle the other tools need. Returns matching brands (with slug and product count) and/or a creator (handle and display name). Do not use for non-beauty entities or general web identity lookup. Then pass the slug to get_brand_reviews or the handle to get_creator_recommendations. If nothing comes back, fall back to search_beauty_products(q=name) to find the entity through a product result.

name.description: The brand or creator name to resolve. Write it as the user wrote it — punctuation, accents, partial names all handled.

type.description: Which entity type to search. Default: 'any' (searches both). Use 'brand' or 'creator' to narrow.

q.description: Free-text search across brand, product name, and shade. Best used for a brand name, a product name, or a brand+product phrase like 'Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun' or 'SKIN1004 Madagascar'. Do NOT pass ingredients here — use the ingredient= param instead. category.description: Top-level aisle, e.g. LIP, HAIR, FRAGRANCE. Use subcategory when you know the product type.

spf.description: true = only products with sun protection (a labelled SPF, or a sunscreen). Use for SPF as a FEATURE: 'lip balm with SPF' → subcategory='lip balm and treatment', spf=true. For a sunscreen itself use subcategory='face sunscreen'.

ingredient.description: Filter by key ingredient. Examples: hyaluronic acid, niacinamide, retinol, centella asiatica, ceramide, azelaic acid, vitamin C.

concern.description: Skin concern to match (best-effort text search). Examples: acne, redness, hyperpigmentation, barrier repair, dryness, sensitivity, oiliness.

max_price_usd.description: Maximum price in USD (best-effort — coverage is partial). Use for budget queries like 'under $30'.

creator_type.description: Filter or prefer creators of a specific type. Examples: dermatologist, makeup artist, esthetician, skincare creator.

verified.description: HARD filter — only products a creator EXPLICITLY verified on camera carry the claim. Comma-separated = AND (must carry all). Valid values: no_white_cast, non_comedogenic, fragrance_free, vegan, cruelty_free, fungal_acne_safe, pregnancy_safe, alcohol_free, oil_free, sulfate_free. Coverage is sparse for vegan / cruelty_free / pregnancy_safe — a product NOT tagged is not necessarily lacking the property, it just means no creator stated it. Use for 'fragrance-free…', 'no white cast', 'fungal-acne safe', 'cruelty-free…'.

origin.description: HARD filter on brand origin. Use for 'best K-beauty SPF' (k_beauty), 'French pharmacy moisturizer' (french_pharmacy), etc.

retailer.description: HARD filter — only products whose brand is verified as carried by this retailer. Examples: Sephora, Ulta, YesStyle, Amazon. Use for 'what can I buy at Sephora'.

formulation.description: HARD filter on product texture/format. Examples: cream, gel, serum, balm, oil, lotion, stick, powder, liquid.

finish.description: HARD filter on makeup finish. Examples: matte, dewy, satin, natural, radiant. Use for 'matte foundation', 'dewy blush'.

skin_tone.description: SOFT re-rank toward products creators matched to a skin tone (shade-range relevance). Use for 'blush for deep skin', 'foundation for fair skin'.

attribute.description: SOFT re-rank toward a creator-stated performance attribute. routine_context.description: SOFT re-rank toward a usage/occasion context creators tied to the product.
